ti.lede: This tab overlays the three reports by keyword (query, journey, cluster) and keeps only what no single report can show. Every number and coordinate is computed automatically, and the six cards below are conclusions that only appear once the three are combined.
ti.readguide.title: How to read this tab — one card = one conclusion that needs all three reports
ti.readguide.m1: M1 Coverage gaps — overlays the three reports to find blind spots none of them caught
ti.readguide.m2: M2 Hub roles — compares how important each of the three lenses considers the same keyword
ti.readguide.m3: M3 Persona × journey — tables who looks for what at which stage, and flags the empty cells in red
ti.readguide.m4: M4 Revenue leaks — finds where high-value searches lose customers along the journey
ti.readguide.m5: M5 Conversion corridors — checks whether keywords searched together actually move from A to B
ti.readguide.m6: M6 Action backlog — scores the five cards together into what to do now, next and later
ti.m1.title: Coverage Gaps — Blind Spots None of the Reports Caught
ti.m1.desc: Keywords that appear in only one report, or in none, once the three are overlaid
ti.m1.plain: In plain terms — this card overlays the three reports to find blind spots: heavily searched terms that the journey and cluster views never picked up.
ti.m1.coverMeter: Share of search volume caught by all three reports at once
ti.m1.gap.qnp: Heavily searched but absent from the journey
ti.m1.gap.qnc: Heavily searched but not grouped into any cluster
ti.m1.gap.snq: Present in the journey and clusters but no search purpose identified
ti.m1.honest: A 'gap' here may be a genuine hole in the market, or simply a difference in what each report covers. Use the coverage share above to tell them apart.
ti.m2.title: Hub Role Mismatch — Genuine Core vs. Half a Hub
ti.m2.desc: How important the same keyword looks through each of the three lenses (journey, cluster, demand)
ti.m2.plain: In plain terms — this card lines up the importance each lens assigns to the same keyword, separating keywords that are core in all three from ones that only stand out in a single view.
ti.m2.honest: The cluster lens approximates importance from how often terms are searched together, so it has measurement limits (treat it as a reference).
ti.m3.title: Persona × Journey — Who Looks for What, and Where
ti.m3.desc: Filled cells (demand) + empty cells (content gaps) + drop-off by stage
ti.m3.plain: In plain terms — this card tables who (which cluster) looks for what at each stage (entry, comparison, decision), and marks in red the empty cells where customers arrive but no content exists.
ti.m3.gapTitle: Demand flows through the neighbouring stages but this cell alone is empty (content gap)
ti.m3.legendHeat: Filled cells: demand (darker = higher commercial intent)
ti.m3.legendGap: Empty cells: demand next door, zero here
ti.m3.legendSlope: Commercial intent trend: rising entry → decision (green) / falling (red)
ti.m4.title: Revenue Leaks — Valuable Searches That Slip Away
ti.m4.desc: Where high commercial-intent searches leak out of the journey, ranked by what to defend first
ti.m4.plain: In plain terms — this card finds the points where customers drop out of the journey on searches that carry real commercial value, and ranks which to plug first.
ti.m4.honest: Leak strength is computed purely from the journey structure (branching and back-tracking) — interpretive labels are not mixed into the score.
ti.m5.title: Conversion Corridors — Searched Together, but Do They Actually Move?
ti.m5.desc: Whether undirected co-search turns into an actual directed journey
ti.m5.plain: In plain terms — this card separates pairs that genuinely move from A to B from pairs where customers abandon ours and leave for a competitor.
ti.m5.honest: Forward and back counts are approximated from journey order, not real clicks. When the sample is thin we mark it honestly as 'inconclusive'.
ti.m6.title: Action Backlog — Now / Next / Later
ti.m6.desc: A prioritised backlog built by scoring the five cards above together
ti.m6.plain: In plain terms — this card folds the five cards above into a single score and lays out what to do now, next and later.
ti.m6.kpiLeak: Leaked search volume you could win back
ti.m6.kpiOrphan: High-intent keywords with no structure behind them
ti.m6.kpiCoverage: Covered by all three reports at once
ti.m6.leakLegendBody: ① dropping out at a journey stage (M3) · ② valuable keywords slipping away (M4) · ③ switching to a competing cluster (M5). These are separate diagnoses.
